Persecutors
pẽr´sē-kū-terz
n. pl. (those who pursue to harm; rendering Hebrew radaph, to pursue)
Latin persequi, to follow after. The Hebrew is simply the pursuer; a persecutor is a man who will not let the righteous go.

Biblical Definition

Jeremiah prays, “remember me, and visit me, and revenge me of my persecutors” (Jer 15:15), and answers his own prayer with faith: “the LORD is with me as a mighty terrible one: therefore my persecutors shall stumble, and they shall not prevail” (Jer 20:11). The psalmist: “Many are my persecutors and mine enemies; yet do I not decline from thy testimonies” (Psa 119:157); “deliver me from my persecutors; for they are stronger than I” (Psa 142:6). God “ordaineth his arrows against the persecutors” (Psa 7:13). Of the exodus: “their persecutors thou threwest into the deeps, as a stone into the mighty waters” (Neh 9:11). Of the fall of Jerusalem: “all her persecutors overtook her between the straits” (Lam 1:3).

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines persecutor as one who persecutes; one who pursues another unjustly and vexatiously, particularly on account of religion.

expand to see more

PERSECUTOR, n. One who persecutes; one who pursues another unjustly and vexatiously, particularly on account of his religious opinions.

Key Scripture

Jer 20:11 — "But the LORD is with me as a mighty terrible one: therefore my persecutors shall stumble, and they shall not prevail: they shall be greatly ashamed; for they shall not prosper: their everlasting confusion shall never be forgotten."

Psa 119:157 — "Many are my persecutors and mine enemies; yet do I not decline from thy testimonies."

Jer 15:15 — "O LORD, thou knowest: remember me, and visit me, and revenge me of my persecutors; take me not away in thy longsuffering: know that for thy sake I have suffered rebuke."

Psa 142:6 — "Attend unto my cry; for I am brought very low: deliver me from my persecutors; for they are stronger than I."

Neh 9:11 — "And thou didst divide the sea before them, so that they went through the midst of the sea on the dry land; and their persecutors thou threwest into the deeps, as a stone into the mighty waters."

Modern Corruption

The persecuted decline from the testimonies to make the persecutors stop, and Psalm 119:157 sets the two clauses against each other on purpose.

expand to see more

“Many are my persecutors and mine enemies; yet do I not decline from thy testimonies.” The verse knows the temptation exactly: persecution's whole purpose is to make the righteous decline — to soften the testimony a little, to leave the offending doctrine unsaid, to buy peace with a small silence — and the psalmist's yet is the refusal. The modern church declines by inches and calls each inch wisdom. Jeremiah shows the alternative to declining, which is not fighting: he asks God to revenge him of his persecutors, and then confesses that the LORD is with him as a mighty terrible one, so that the persecutors will stumble on their own. The vengeance is God's, the testimony is the prophet's, and neither is surrendered.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew radaph (H7291), to pursue, chase, persecute; participle, a pursuer, persecutor.

expand to see more

Hebrew radaph (H7291), participle — persecutors, pursuers; Psalm 7:13, 119:157, 142:6, Jeremiah 15:15, 17:18, 20:11, Lamentations 1:3, 4:19, Nehemiah 9:11.

Usage

"“Many are my persecutors and mine enemies; yet do I not decline from thy testimonies” — the refusal."

"“Therefore my persecutors shall stumble” — Jeremiah's answer to his own prayer."

"“Their persecutors thou threwest into the deeps” — the Red Sea remembered."
